candidates.original_title: Education and Catch-Up in the Industrial Revolution
candidates.description: Education had a positive causal effect on overall Prussian industrialisation during the first phase of industrialisation, measured in 1849.
candidates.citation_sentence: Becker, Hornung and Woessmann (henceforth BHW) argue that such education made an important contribution to the industrialisation of Prussia (BHW 2011).
candidates.notes: The replication's IV estimate is negative and statistically significant after accounting for regional effects and applying systematic model selection. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Education and Catch-Up in the Industrial Revolution
candidates.description: Education had a positive causal effect on metal-sector industrialisation during the first phase of Prussian industrialisation.
candidates.citation_sentence: Becker, Hornung and Woessmann (henceforth BHW) argue that such education made an important contribution to the industrialisation of Prussia (BHW 2011).
candidates.notes: The replication finds a large, statistically significant negative IV effect in the metal sector, but the authors do not explicitly label it a reversal. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
